name: Solari

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Professional sandbox rate only. Desktop VM adds $0.02/h; not included in this mode.

plans.name: Professional
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Only with the Free-tier rates ($0.0525/vCPU-h, $0.0165/GB-h); bind via a mode with plans:["Free"].

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom fee; published rates $0.0175/vCPU-h, $0.0055/GB-h 'unless your contract sets different ones'; HIPAA; unlimited session.

caveats: Public tiered list rates, shared credits cover browsers, sandboxes and desktop VMs. Engine card represents Professional sandbox only; other tier rates retained as raw regimes because freely combining tier-specific rates with any plan would underprice. Professional only permits 10 concurrent sandboxes.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

isolation:"shared" tier (process tree in a 4-vCPU VM shared with your own shared sandboxes; cpu<=4, memMb<=2048, default 512) is described as 'cheaper' but has no published separate rate; 'hardened' = dedicated with all outbound blocked. Parked sandboxes (parkAfterMs) keep their concurrency slot and appear to keep billing; only full pause stops billing. Desktop VMs add $0.02/h for the live screen.

fleet.tiers: Sandboxes/VMs: Free 1, Starter 2, Professional 10, Enterprise 50+. Browsers separately 3/20/150/150+.
fleet.notes: Default refers to compute sandboxes, not browser concurrency. 10 machines requires Professional, 50 Enterprise, 300/1,000 custom confirmation. Stealth browsers have a separate lower 0/10/50/75 ceiling.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When that time passes with no activity, lifecycle decides what happens: onTimeout: "pause" (the default) saves its state and pauses it, while onTimeout: "kill" shuts it down. If you don't set timeoutMs , it defaults to 30 minutes.
snapshot_auto.note: Default idle timeout (30 min) pauses and saves full state (memory + disk, 'a full pause restores from durable storage'); resumes on connect(). Opt-in extras: hibernateAfterParkedMs escalates a park to a full pause, checkpointEveryMs takes periodic durable checkpoints (min 60 s). Same for desktop VMs.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: snapshot(name?) saves the machine's current state and gives you back a snapshot id. The machine keeps running the whole time
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included ('it carries its own complete disk and memory image'); revert(snapshotId) rewinds in place; create({fromSnapshot}) boots any number of new machines (fork); snapshots can be promoted to templates. Machine must be running (409 on paused). Works for sandboxes and VMs. $0.05/GB-month above 10 GB from 2026-10-01.

egress_allowlist.quote: "hardened" is the same, with all outbound network blocked.
egress_allowlist.note: Only an all-or-nothing no-internet mode (isolation:"hardened"); no domain or IP allow/deny lists documented.

ingress_rules.quote: The URL is signed: it carries a one-hour pt_token query parameter, and the response also returns that token separately as preview.token .
ingress_rules.note: Ports exposed only on request via previewUrl(port) / GET /sandboxes/:id/ports/:port; hostname <label>-<port>.preview.getsolari.com; 401 without a valid token. No IP allowlists or security groups.

guest_firewall.note: isolation:"dedicated"/"hardened" is a microVM of your own (docs); examples run apt-get as the default user, so root. isolation:"shared" is a namespace+cgroup context in a shared VM; NET_ADMIN unknown.

volume_attach.quote: A volume is durable storage that outlives any single machine. Create one once, then attach it to a sandbox at start-up and read and write it at a path of your choosing.
volume_attach.note: Beta; sandboxes only (all isolation modes), not yet desktops. Attach at create time only. Backed by GCS via host-side gcsfuse.

volume_shared.quote: A machine can mount several volumes at once, and the same volume can be attached to many machines.
volume_shared.note: Read-write from multiple machines ('a folder of data that many machines read and write over time'); gcsfuse object-storage semantics, no documented locking/consistency guarantees.

anti_bot.quote: Stealth mode makes your browser look like an ordinary person's, so it gets through sites that block bots.

captcha_solving.quote: Solari solves common captcha widgets for you: reCaptcha v2/v3, hCaptcha, and Cloudflare Turnstile.
captcha_solving.note: Requires stealth: true; billed $0.005-$0.01/solve depending on plan.

egress_ip_type.quote: Route your browser through an IP in the country you choose. Pick from three kinds of IP (rotating residential, static ISP, and mobile)...
egress_ip_type.note: The residential/static/mobile proxy tiers are a browser-session add-on (sessions.create({proxy})), not the default egress for sandboxes/VMs. Absent a proxy, machines egress on ordinary cloud datacenter IPs; no datacenter IP details (static vs shared) are published.

ssh.quote: pty.create opens one you can write to, resize, and read from. It's what powers the console's web terminal.
ssh.note: not offered: access is via the SDK/API control channel (commands, PTY, files) rather than a standard SSH server/protocol; no SSH endpoint or key-based SSH access is documented.

fork_running.quote: snapshot(name?) saves the machine's current state and gives you back a snapshot id. The machine keeps running the whole time
fork_running.note: create({fromSnapshot}) then boots any number of new machines from that snapshot while the original keeps running untouched.

wake_on_request.quote: onTimeout: "pause" (the default) saves its state and pauses it... resumes on connect().
wake_on_request.note: A paused/idle sandbox or VM automatically resumes the moment connect() is called again.

persistent_disk.note: There is no separate stop/start cycle with a durable disk: killing a sandbox/VM terminates it. Data only survives via pause (full state save/resume), an explicit snapshot, or a separately attached volume — not as an always-on persistent root disk.

live_resize.quote: Ask for more than that and the create is rejected with a 400 — it is not quietly reduced. Set cpu and memMb at create time.
live_resize.note: Size (cpu/memMb) is fixed at create time and only 'sticks' across pause/resume/snapshot; there is no API to change CPU/RAM of a running machine in place.

agent_harnesses.quote: base: the standard headless sandbox (the sandbox default). default / workstation: the standard Ubuntu desktop — XFCE with Chrome, LibreOffice and VS Code.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: only plain OS/desktop templates (base, workstation) are documented; no Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode or other coding-agent template is listed.

harness_api.quote: A sandbox is a machine for running code and automation, with no screen: run commands, execute code that keeps its state, watch files, and snapshot and fork.
harness_api.note: not offered: the API drives generic commands/PTY/code-exec, not a first-party API for prompting/streaming a preinstalled coding agent.

own_agent_api.quote: Cloud infrastructure for agents and automation: stealthy Chrome browsers, full Linux VMs, and fast code sandboxes.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Solari provides infrastructure (browsers/VMs/sandboxes) that your agent drives; it does not ship its own first-party browsing/computer-use/research agent with a task API.

mcp_server.quote: The Solari MCP server exposes 27 tools over the Model Context Protocol.
mcp_server.note: Hosted endpoint at https://mcp.getsolari.com/mcp or local via `npx @solarisdk/mcp`.

lang_python.quote: Python solari-sandbox, solari-desktop Full: computer-use, PTY, viewer, snapshots
lang_python.note: TypeScript and Python SDKs are at full parity; runCode also executes Python inside sandboxes.

lang_node.quote: TypeScript @solarisdk/sandbox, @solarisdk/desktop Full: computer-use, PTY, viewer, snapshots

public_ipv4.quote: The URL is signed: it carries a one-hour pt_token query parameter, and the response also returns that token separately as preview.token.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: exposed ports are reached only via signed preview URLs (<label>-<port>.preview.getsolari.com), not a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine.

egress_http_rules.quote: "hardened" is the same, with all outbound network blocked.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: only an all-or-nothing outbound block (isolation: "hardened") is documented; no HTTP method/path-level egress rule engine exists.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials are passed per-call and never touch a shell, so there is nothing to escape or inject.
secret_proxy.note: not offered: this applies narrowly to the git namespace's own credential params, not a general first-party HTTP proxy that injects secrets for arbitrary or AI-provider APIs. Standard access is via API key / env vars.

static_egress_ip.quote: tier "static" ("static": one fixed IP that stays the same all session)
static_egress_ip.note: The fixed/static IP tier is a browser-session proxy add-on, not a static outbound IP for sandboxes/VMs; no static egress IP for sandboxes/VMs is documented.

gpu.quote: Sandboxes & VMs Billed by size (vCPUs and memory), so a small machine costs a fraction of a large one.
gpu.note: not offered: pricing/sizing is CPU+RAM only; no GPU instance type is listed anywhere in the docs.

windows.quote: VMs default to the standard Ubuntu desktop.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — VMs and sandboxes are Linux (Ubuntu) microVMs only.

macos.quote: full Linux VMs, and fast code sandboxes
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Solari's compute product is explicitly Linux VMs/sandboxes.

self_host.quote: Cloud infrastructure for agents and automation: stealthy Chrome browsers, full Linux VMs, and fast code sandboxes. All of it runs on hardware-isolated microVMs, behind one API key.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Solari is a hosted multi-tenant SaaS (api.getsolari.com/console.getsolari.com) with no self-hosted deployment option documented.

byoc.quote: Cloud infrastructure for agents and automation... All of it runs on hardware-isolated microVMs, behind one API key.
byoc.note: not offered: no bring-your-own-cloud / deploy-into-your-account option is documented; capacity runs on Solari's own fleet.

open_source.quote: TypeScript npm install @solarisdk/sandbox ... Python pip install solari-sandbox
open_source.note: Only client SDKs are distributed as packages; no OSI license or public repo for the core sandbox/VM/browser engine is referenced anywhere in the docs.

sso.quote: Multiple Google accounts can be members of the same organization and share everything.
sso.note: not offered: only Google-account sign-in and email invite links are documented; no SAML/OIDC single sign-on is mentioned.

eu_data_residency.quote: Region SDK value Connect to Status US West (N. California) us-west api.getsolari.com Available
eu_data_residency.note: Only one region (US West, N. California) is currently available; no EU region is listed.

max_session_h.quote: Max session time 1 hour 5 hours 24 hours Unlimited
max_session_h.note: 24h applies to the Professional plan, which is the plan bound to the card's primary on-demand mode. Enterprise is contractually unlimited; Free=1h, Starter=5h.

image_oci.quote: const image = Image.base("ubuntu:22.04").kind("sandbox") // "sandbox" (headless) or "desktop" (with a screen) .aptInstall(["ffmpeg", "poppler-utils"]).pipInstall(["pandas", "pdfplumber"]).runCommands("mkdir -p /work").env({ HF_HOME: "/work/.hf" }).workdir("/work") // Build it and wait until it's ready to use. const tpl = await templates.build(image, { name: "media-tools" })
image_oci.note: Custom templates are built server-side from a named base OS plus an apt/pip/run/env/workdir builder DSL (or Image.fromTemplate("workstation")); there is no documented way to start a machine from an arbitrary pre-built Docker/OCI image or registry reference, and uploading local files into a build isn't supported yet ('Uploading files from your own computer (addLocalFile()/addLocalDir()) isn't supported yet; a recipe that uses it is turned away when you build.'). custom_image:true is correct (you can customize the image via templates) but image_oci:false is also correct since you can't bring your own container/OCI image.
